articles.title: 5 ways India is kicking car safety into top gear with Bharat NCAP 2.0: What buyers need to know
articles.summary: Bharat NCAP 2.0, planned for October 2027, will look beyond what happens when a car crashes.
articles.body: Bharat NCAP 2.0, planned for October 2027, will look beyond what happens when a car crashes. The proposed system will examine the entire safety chain: from how a vehicle helps avoid a collision to how well it protects occupants, pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and what happens after an accident.Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari announced the proposed timeline at the SIAM Annual Convention in September 2026. The second phase is being planned as the first phase of Bharat New Car Assessment Programme, or Bharat NCAP, approaches the end of its current cycle.According to the ministry of road transport and highways’ draft AIS-197 Revision 1, the first phase of Bharat NCAP began on October 1, 2023 and is valid until September 30, 2027. The draft revision has been prepared as the framework for Bharat NCAP 2.0.The proposed changes could make the safety rating a much broader measure of a car’s performance, not just in a crash, but before, during and after one.What is Bharat NCAP?Bharat NCAP is India’s own vehicle crash-testing and safety-rating programme. It was formally launched by the ministry of road transport and highways in August 2023 and became operational from October 1, 2023.The programme applies to type-approved passenger vehicles in the M1 category with a gross vehicle weight of less than 3.5 tonnes. It is voluntary, which means manufacturers can offer eligible vehicles for assessment.The programme is anchored by the Central Institute of Road Transport (CIRT), while testing is carried out through designated agencies with the required infrastructure.At its core, Bharat NCAP gives car buyers a common safety benchmark. A vehicle must already meet mandatory regulatory requirements to be sold in India. Bharat NCAP goes a step further by putting eligible vehicles through specified tests and awarding them a rating of between one and five stars.The idea is fairly simple: instead of looking only at a car’s price, design or features, buyers get an additional reference point to understand how the vehicle performs in standardised safety tests.The government has also positioned the programme as a way to encourage manufacturers to improve vehicle safety and strengthen the safety standards of cars made in India.How does the current Bharat NCAP system work?The existing programme broadly assesses three areas:Adult Occupant Protection (AOP)Child Occupant Protection (COP)Safety Assist Technologies (SAT)Vehicles are subjected to prescribed crash tests and other assessments. Their performance across these parameters is then used to arrive at the overall star rating.The current framework includes a 64 kmph offset frontal impact test, a 50 kmph side movable deformable barrier test and a pole side impact test, among other checks prescribed under AIS-197.The assessment therefore goes beyond simply asking whether the passenger compartment remains intact.Adult Occupant Protection examines the risk of injury to adults in different crash conditions and seating positions. Child Occupant Protection looks at the protection offered to younger passengers, including the use and installation of child restraint systems.Safety Assist Technologies, meanwhile, covers technologies designed to help prevent crashes or reduce their severity.Why are adult and child safety assessed separately?A car may offer different levels of protection to adults and children, so Bharat NCAP evaluates the two separately.The adult assessment focuses on occupant protection during prescribed crash scenarios, while the child assessment considers how effectively younger occupants are protected and how child restraint systems work within the vehicle.This also means that a car’s overall star rating is not simply a score from one crash test. It reflects performance across several safety parameters.For consumers, the individual scores can therefore provide more information than looking at the star rating alone.Who tests the cars?Bharat NCAP is anchored by CIRT, with testing carried out through designated testing agencies that have the required facilities.The wider automotive testing ecosystem includes agencies such as the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and the International Centre for Automotive Technology (ICAT).Manufacturers submit eligible vehicles for assessment under the programme. The existing framework specifies procedures around the variant selected for testing, including provisions concerning the base variant of a model.That distinction matters when reading a Bharat NCAP result. A rating should not automatically be assumed to apply to every variant of a model unless the official assessment covers those variants.Bharat NCAP ratingsBharat NCAP ratings range from one to five stars. A higher rating indicates stronger performance under the programme’s prescribed assessment criteria.But a five-star rating is not a guarantee that occupants will escape injury in every real-world crash. NCAP testing is conducted under standardised conditions and is intended to provide a basis for comparing vehicle safety performance.It is also important to distinguish Bharat NCAP from the mandatory certification requirements for selling a vehicle in India.Bharat NCAP is voluntary and is designed to provide consumers with additional information beyond the mandatory regulatory framework. A vehicle being tested or rated under Bharat NCAP should therefore not be confused with regulatory approval.Since its launch, Bharat NCAP has increasingly become part of the safety conversation around new car launches. The ratings have also become a factor in how manufacturers present their vehicles to consumers, particularly as safety becomes a more visible consideration in the passenger-vehicle market.So, what changes with Bharat NCAP 2.0?This is where the proposed second phase takes a much wider approach.The draft AIS-197 Revision 1 divides Bharat NCAP 2.0 into five safety verticals:Safe drivingCrash avoidanceCrash protectionVulnerable road user protectionPost-crash safetyThe change is significant because the current system focuses mainly on occupant protection and safety-assist technologies, while the proposed framework looks at the complete safety chain.The draft framework uses a 100-point assessment structure, with Crash Protection accounting for 55% of the assessment. The remaining weightage covers the other safety areas.In other words, the crash itself will still be a major part of the rating, but it will no longer be the only part of the safety story.Five crash tests in the proposed new frameworkBharat NCAP 2.0 proposes expanding the Crash Protection assessment to five mandatory crash tests:64 kmph offset frontal impact against a deformable barrier50 kmph frontal impact against a full-width rigid barrier50 kmph lateral impact against a mobile deformable barrier32 kmph oblique side impact against a rigid pole50 kmph rear impact against a mobile rigid barrierAdult and child occupant protection will continue to be assessed separately.The addition of full-width frontal and rear-impact tests means the proposed system will examine crash scenarios beyond the core tests in the existing framework.That gives the second phase a wider testing footprint and allows different types of impacts to form part of the overall safety assessment.Not just about surviving crashOne of the biggest differences in Bharat NCAP 2.0 is that the programme is designed to look at what happens before a crash as well.Crash Avoidance is one of the five proposed verticals. It focuses on technologies and vehicle characteristics that can help prevent a collision or reduce its severity.Safe Driving is another proposed category, widening the assessment beyond the vehicle’s passive protection features.Together, these categories shift the focus from simply asking, “How well does this car perform when it crashes?” to a broader question: “How does this vehicle contribute to safety across different stages of a road incident?”Bharat NCAP 2.0 also proposes a separate Vulnerable Road User Protection category. This brings pedestrians and other vulnerable road users more directly into the safety assessment.The proposed framework also asks a different question: what happens once the collision has taken place?Post-Crash Safety is one of the five proposed assessment areas. Minister Gadkari described Bharat NCAP 2.0 as covering the entire safety chain, including post-crash evacuation and care. “We are going to evaluate the entire crash chain,” Gadkari said, adding that new technologies developed globally as well as by startups would be considered under the programme.This means the assessment is intended to extend beyond the instant of impact and examine safety considerations in the period immediately after a crash.It adds another layer to the programme’s approach: avoiding the crash where possible, protecting people during the impact, and addressing safety after the collision.What does Bharat NCAP mean for car buyers?For buyers, Bharat NCAP offers an additional way to compare cars beyond mandatory safety requirements.A consumer can look at a vehicle’s overall rating as well as its adult and child protection performance and the safety technologies considered in the assessment.The rating is not meant to replace other factors involved in buying a car. Price, size, fuel efficiency, features, driving requirements and other considerations remain relevant, but the proposed 2.0 framework would expand that information further.Buyers could eventually have a broader picture of how a car performs across crash protection, crash avoidance, safe driving, vulnerable-road-user protection and post-crash safety.Bharat NCAP is one part of a much larger road-safety challenge, focusing on the structure of vehicles. Vehicle design and safety technology can influence the outcome of a crash, but they cannot address every reason why accidents happen.The ministry has identified several factors associated with road crashes, including speeding, mobile-phone use, drunken driving, wrong-side driving, lane indiscipline, jumping red lights and failure to use helmets and seat belts. Vehicle condition, road conditions and weather can also play a role.Government data recorded 1,68,491 road accident fatalities in 2022.Bharat NCAP therefore addresses one part of this wider equation: the safety performance of vehicles. Its proposed second phase would broaden that role by looking at what a vehicle can do to help avoid crashes, how it protects people when a crash occurs, how it protects vulnerable road users and what happens afterwards.The bottom lineThe current Bharat NCAP phase remains valid until September 30, 2027. The government has proposed introducing Bharat NCAP 2.0 from October 2027, with the draft AIS-197 Revision 1 serving as the framework for the next phase.The proposed transition would take India’s vehicle safety-rating system from a relatively focused crash and occupant-protection programme to a broader safety assessment.The familiar one-to-five-star rating would remain the consumer-facing language of vehicle safety, but the assessment behind it is set to become much more comprehensive.The bigger shift is in the question Bharat NCAP is trying to answer. Instead of looking only at how a car performs when it is involved in a crash, the proposed system would examine the vehicle’s safety journey from avoiding a collision to protecting occupants and vulnerable road users, and supporting safety after the crash.That could give Indian car buyers a wider set of safety information to consider when choosing their next vehicle.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: RANDOM MUSING | The lesbian bar outrage shows why Donald Trump won America
articles.summary: One was oddly reminded of Onoda after coming across the Boston ‘lesbian bar story’ that is every product manager’s wet dream: a story published in the Boston Globe that went so viral that it led to thousands of subscriptions for what seemed a rather nondescript story but is an elegant outpost of woke America’s last bastion.
articles.body: Plato’s Allegory of the Cave is the notion that none of us can truly perceive a world beyond our availability heuristic, which shapes our perception of reality. In simpler terms, Plato imagines that if people are chained in a cave and can only view those shadows, those shadows become their reality. The best pop-cultural manifestation of Plato’s Allegory was The Matrix, where all unfree characters are in a dream-like sleep and have no idea they are living inside a computer programme.The real-life analogy is anyone who consumes so much propaganda that no amount of rationalising, to borrow a line from Dr House, would change their opinion.Perhaps the most extreme version of that is the epochal tale of Hiroo Onoda, a Japanese soldier stationed in the Philippines at the fag end of World War II, who “fought” for thirty years and refused to lay down his arms.Once the island was overtaken by Allied forces, Onoda and his comrades escaped into the jungle, where they survived on coconuts, banana peels and stolen rice.While his peers shuffled off their mortal coil, Onoda kept fighting – despite evidence to the contrary, which he dismissed as American propaganda – and it wasn’t till 1974, nearly 30 years after he was sent to fight, that the soldier out of time laid down his arms.One was oddly reminded of Onoda after coming across the Boston ‘lesbian bar story’ that is every product manager’s wet dream: a story published in the Boston Globe that went so viral that it led to thousands of subscriptions for what seemed a rather nondescript story but is an elegant outpost of woke America’s last bastion.For those who don’t monitor the situation online and believe in touching grass, here’s the CliffsNotes version.A lesbian bar in Greenfield, Massachusetts, made a slight change to its Saturday-night mask policy that led to a culture war so elaborate it would have been rejected by South Park for being too obvious.Last Ditch, a lesbian bar on record, is an “aggressively inclusive queer space” where patrons are required to wear KN95 masks in 2026. It turns nobody away for being broke and explicitly welcomes “dykes, transsexuals, gender freaks, workers, and their friends”. All these admirable intentions soon encountered humanity’s oldest ideological opponent: rent.Customers disappeared, staff couldn’t be paid and co-founder Jackie Matellian worked four jobs and lived in her truck for six months while carrying the responsibility for a $50,000 business loan. So, the bar decided to make the smallest concession to Mammon: Saturday nights would be mask-optional.The response is exactly what you would expect if someone replaced a Pride flag with a flag of Israel.What followed is the perfect living example of what can be called the Toaster F**** Syndrome.For those who don’t know, the theory is simple. Pre-internet, if someone wanted to perform coitus with a piece of electrical equipment and expressed that desire, they would be told by their peers that it was imbecilic to want to f*** a toaster. But post-World Wide Web, when someone expressed that desire, they would find thousands of other individuals who would soon form a community and try and convince everyone that it was the new normal.After the Instagram post, all the toaster f***** were out in full force.Commenters accused the bar of ableism, eugenics and facilitating mass disability. One hoped it would be firebombed. The bar apologised on Instagram, which made it even worse because the apology graphic had no alt-text and was thus ‘triggering’ for visually impaired folks, prompting another round of accusations of ableism.One activist called Soe Noire, who is a lesbian and uses ‘he/him’ pronouns, accused the debt-ridden founder Matellian of producing “White THEY THEM Tears”. The internet did its best, which saw Last Ditch defend Soe Noire, accuse the Globe of “abysmal journalism” and ask everyone to donate to ‘his’ Cash App and Venmo because ‘he’ was being harassed.All this because a lesbian bar decided to relax its mask mandate for one day in 2026.But honestly, Last Ditch Bar sounds appropriately named because it feels like a time capsule, harking back to the good ol’ days of ‘peak woke’ America.Now, historians differ over the year when America hit ‘peak woke’, but most agree it was between 2019 and 2021, when Trump’s first term ended.Fauci’s words on masks and everything else became the gospel truth. Everyone was listening and learning. Suggesting the lab leak theory was plausible was deemed racism. George Floyd was beatified and put on par with Martin Luther King Jr, while Black Lives Matter became the most important religion on earth. The police clearly needed to be defunded.Read: ‘Dr’ Donald Trump, Tylenol, and why Americans don’t trust the ‘science’ anymoreIt was a time when, if you sent a Slack message that read, “Guys, I am stuck in a lift”, Slack would auto-correct you and point out that “Guys” was gendered language.Across the Atlantic, a fantastical fabulist named Jason Arday became Cambridge’s youngest Black professor because suddenly every institution of note needed to highlight their allegiance to the woke cause, and JK Rowling became the most hated person in the world because she had the audacity to point out that sex was real and that perhaps biological men shouldn’t be allowed into sex-segregated places.The problem was that this particular cultural revolution became the Democratic Party’s wider brand, and the Republicans discovered they could attach the most ridiculous views of blue-haired Karens to the Democratic Party.The warning signs were there for all to see.As Virginia Congresswoman Abigail Spanberger said during a private Democratic caucus call: if Democrats didn’t believe in defunding the police, they needed to stop allowing the phrase to define them.Even as the Dems celebrated Trump’s removal, they were paving the way for his return, alienating normies who didn’t want their children to share bathrooms with people in drag, men to play women’s sports or drag queens in children’s classrooms.The messaging became so bad that voters instead chose the former reality star whose first term had already been the presidential equivalent of a supernova explosion.In 2008, Barack Obama built something extraordinary, a grand coalition for all Americans. Obama won independents, suburban voters, Catholics and large chunks of the political middle. Democrats and Democrat-leaning voters constituted 55% of registered voters in Pew’s measurements that year. Republicans, on the other hand, made up 39%.By the final quarter of 2024, Obama’s great coalition was dead.Gallup found Republicans and Republican-leaning independents ahead of Democrats and Democratic leaners by 47% to 43% among US adults, the high-water mark of a remarkable reversal from the Obama years.Read: How Barack Obama ‘birthed’ Donald Trump and MAGASomewhere along the way, Hope and Change had become Please State Your Pronouns. The voice became shriller and shriller, requiring everyone to have an opinion on everything irrespective of whether it mattered.One became a bigot simply by questioning whether a drag queen should be there in a kid’s class or if a trans artist should promote a product mainly targeting straight men. The Democrats handed the Republicans the culture war on a platter.Read: Jimmy Kimmel ‘cancelled’ – comical or tragic?Trump’s campaign eventually reduced years of this cultural resentment to perhaps the most devastating political advertisement of the 2024 election: “Kamala is for they/them. President Trump is for you.” Famous last words for the Democratic Party and even the world, which continues to pay for a political party’s complete suspension of disbelief in handing the nuclear arsenal and the mantle of leader of the free world to the most craven and explicitly corrupt president of America. His vacillating foreign policy decisions, from random tariffs to meaningless wars, made everyone’s life worse: Americans, America’s allies and America’s enemies.Now, with the midterms approaching, America has shown clear signs of moving on from the woke fever dream.The Economist notes that while “Woke 1” was about identity, race, gender, language and privilege, “Woke 2”, championed by the likes of Zohran Mamdani, is centred on class and economics: wages, rent, housing and things that actually matter to real people. The political question has shifted from “Who are you?” to “What can you afford?”If “Woke 1” was essentially identity-based social justice, “Woke 2” is class-based economic populism.Read: Why Zohran Mamdani will find it hard to be another Barack ObamaBut the Last Ditch outrage was a reminder of how insane the peak woke era used to be and the culture war that ensued.For what it’s worth, after World War II, Onoda was finally convinced to lay down his arms when his former commanding officer was flown into the Philippines to convince him that the war was indeed over. Perhaps Barack Obama, the last great commanding officer of the troops of Woke America, can make a trip to the Last Ditch bar to convince them that the culture war, and COVID, are over and to lay down the masks.But there’s a catch.Unlike Onoda, all those involved in the Last Ditch fight have access to the internet. Now the folks chained in Plato’s cave have Wi-Fi and a smartphone that tells them the shadows they see are reality. And no amount of rationalising will convince them otherwise.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: The release of US national Matthew Aaron VanDyke, who was arrested by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in March in a case involving an alleged terror conspiracy linked to Myanmar-based ethnic armed groups, has triggered a political row, with the Congress questioning the circumstances of his release and alleging that US diplomatic pressure influenced the outcome."Our compromised PM has does it again. The PM has failed to protect India’s elections, institutions and our national security," Congress said in a post on X.VanDyke and six Ukrainian nationals were arrested by the NIA on March 13. According to the agency's allegations, the accused had entered India and travelled to restricted areas in the Northeast before crossing into Myanmar, where they allegedly came into contact with ethnic armed organisations and were involved in drone-warfare training. The NIA had initially registered the case under provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).The agency's March court submissions alleged that the accused supported anti-India insurgent groups. The NIA later told a Delhi court that the seven foreign nationals were allegedly linked to a drone attack on a civilian aircraft in Myanmar, although the investigation remained underway.The case took a fresh turn on September 8, when the NIA filed a chargesheet against the seven under Sections 21 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, without invoking UAPA provisions in the chargesheet. The agency said the UAPA investigation had not been closed and that a supplementary chargesheet could be filed if further offences were established.A Delhi court subsequently granted VanDyke default bail, observing that the chargesheet was "piecemeal" while the investigation into the UAPA offences remained pending. The 180-day statutory period for completing the investigation had also elapsed.On September 24, the court allowed VanDyke and the six Ukrainian nationals to travel to their respective countries for a month, subject to conditions. The court also released their passports.Congress has alleged that the development followed US pressure and questioned whether diplomatic intervention played a role. The party has also raised questions over how the foreign nationals obtained Indian visas and were able to travel to restricted areas of the Northeast before allegedly crossing into Myanmar.The government has maintained that the terror investigation against VanDyke and the other accused remains open. articles.title: Strengthening nor'easter threatens East Coast with floods, outages
articles.summary: A powerful nor'easter is moving up the East Coast, bringing heavy rain, coastal flooding and potential power outages. Air travel may also be affected.
articles.body:
A strengthening nor'easter moving up the East Coast on Sept. 25 is expected to last through the weekend, with deteriorating conditions spawning even stronger winds and coastal flooding.

The large-scale low-pressure storm system will bring more rain from North Carolina to New England, with significant impacts expected in the Outer Banks, New Jersey, Boston and New York City.

Power outages are likely, according to AccuWeather's latest forecast .

Nor'easters are named for the strong northeasterly winds that blow in from the Atlantic Ocean and across coastal states.

The strong storm, taking place through the weekend's full moon, will raise tide levels and lead to major coastal flooding, meteorologists predict. Pounding surf will cause "extensive beach erosion" from North Carolina to southern Maine. Dangerous rip currents will extend as far south as Florida's Atlantic coast, according to the forecast.

"This storm may be remembered for its destructive coastal flooding and severe beach erosion, especially along eastern Long Island and the Massachusetts coast," AccuWeather Chief Meteorologist Jon Porter said.

Coastal flood warnings are in effect for Virginia Beach, Virginia; Dover, Delaware; and Atlantic City, New Jersey. The most severe flooding expected from the northern Outer Banks to the southern New Jersey shore.

Flooding will be worse around high tide through the night of Sept. 25 in much of the mid-Atlantic region.

Some airlines are offering flexibility to travelers who could be impacted. The following carriers have waivers in place for weather along the East Coast:

Water levels will be 2 to 3 feet above the average monthly tide level, AccuWeather reported, with some locations approaching more than 6 feet.

"The worst conditions are forecast for southeastern Virginia, where water will become trapped at the lower end of the Chesapeake Bay, causing backups along the region's tidal rivers," Accuweather wrote in a Sept. 25 post. "Areas in Virginia Beach, Norfolk and Newport News, Virginia, will be inundated for hours at a time."

Near the New Jersey coast, tidal flooding will continue through the weekend in Virginia. Tides are expected to be 2-3 feet above the monthly average, with some areas 4-5 feet above average throughout the northern New Jersey coast through southeastern New York.

Tides are expected to gradually decrease throughout the mid-Atlantic coast starting on Sept. 27.

Southeastern New England will also bear the brunt of the storm starting Sept. 25 through the evening of Sept. 28.

The worst of the storm is expected from the evening of Sept. 25 through the evening or Sept. 26 in Rhode Island, central and eastern Massachusetts, Connecticut, Long Island, New York, southeastern New Hampshire and the southern Maine coast.

Natalie Neysa Alund covers breaking and trending news for USA TODAY. Reach her at nalund@usatoday.com and follow her on Twitter @nataliealund.

articles.title: Supreme Court restores Trump's mass voter verification system
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Sept 25 (Reuters) - The US Supreme Court revived on Friday an expanded immigration database that President Donald Trump's administration said aim...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Sept 25 (Reuters) - The US Supreme Court revived on Friday an expanded immigration database that President Donald Trump's administration said aims to combat voting by noncitizens but critics contend could disenfranchise eligible voters.

The justices granted the Justice Department's request to block a judge's order that had stopped state officials ‌from using Social Security numbers and other information to conduct sweeping checks of the citizenship status of registered voters against federal records.

The court has a 6-3 conservative majority. ‌Its three liberal justices dissented from Friday's order.

The majority said the plaintiffs' arguments likely fail because federal law expressly authorizes the Department of Homeland Security to request and receive information relating to citizenship and immigration status from other agencies, ​including the Social Security Administration.

The administration's data-sharing arrangement is one in a series of actions boosting the federal government's involvement in voting ahead of November's midterm elections in which Trump's fellow Republicans seek to maintain control of Congress. The U.S. Constitution gives individual states the primary authority to run and administer elections.

The Department of Homeland Security last year redesigned a federal database known as the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements, or SAVE, used to verify a person's citizenship and immigration status. The revamp allowed users to search many records at a time and to conduct searches using individuals' Social Security ‌numbers.

Since then, several Republican-led states have compared their voter lists to ⁠the database, and some voters flagged as potential noncitizens have had their registrations canceled.

Critics say such election-related actions by Republicans are driven less by concerns over election security than by an attempt to gain political advantage by narrowing the electorate, risking the disenfranchisement of eligible, often Democratic-leaning voters.

Trump has ⁠carried out hardline policies toward immigration and has made false claims of widespread voting fraud including in his 2020 election loss to Democratic former President Joe Biden.

Advocacy groups that sued to block the revised SAVE system said that the new approach has resulted in people who were wrongfully identified as noncitizens being kicked off voter rolls. They have argued that SAVE can be outdated, meaning immigrants who have become naturalized ​US ​citizens and are thus eligible to vote are sometimes labeled as noncitizens.

The modified system's overall error rate is ​not publicly known. The Department of Homeland Security and Justice Department did ‌not provide that information when asked.

Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, which represents the plaintiffs, called Friday's decision "profoundly disappointing," saying it puts Americans "at risk of being unlawfully targeted by the administration's unreliable voter purge database weeks before the midterm elections."

In a dissent on Friday that was joined by her two fellow liberal justices, Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson wrote that "the harm caused by burdening or disenfranchising even a few lawful voters outweighs the nonexistent harm that the government experiences when it is prevented from taking an action that it likely lacks the authority to take."

In their Supreme Court filing, the advocacy groups cited a Travis County, Texas, election official who said 25% of the system's noncitizen matches there involved people who had already proven their US citizenship, ‌and news reports finding that at least 81% of the system's responses in St. Louis County, Missouri, were ​erroneous.

The voting rights group League of Women Voters and privacy rights group Electronic Privacy Information Center sued in ​September 2025 to block the Trump administration's modified system. They said that the revamp ​violated federal privacy and other U.S. laws.

In a June ruling blocking the revamped database, US District Judge Sparkle Sooknanan in Washington, D.C., said the system ‌was haphazardly assembled and contained unreliable citizenship data.

"All in all, the federal ​government has knowingly trampled on the privacy rights of ​American citizens in a manner that threatens the sacred right to vote," Sooknanan wrote. "This court cannot stand idly by while that happens."

The US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit in a 2-1 ruling on September 4 declined to halt Sooknanan's ruling, prompting the administration's request to the Supreme Court.

In a Supreme Court filing, Justice ​Department lawyers called the judge's order "indefensible," arguing that it "threatens the integrity" ‌of the midterm elections.

Texas, which intervened in the case in support of the administration, has disputed claims that the system is unreliable.

Due to separate litigation in Florida, ​the Trump administration has been able to continue using its modified SAVE system in the Republican-led states of Florida, Iowa, Indiana and Ohio.

(Reporting by John Kruzel; ​with additional reporting by Andrew Chung in New York; Editing by Will Dunham and Daniel Wallis)

articles.title: Around 170 volunteers remove 43,000 pounds of trash from San Antonio dumping site after years of complaints; property was a homeless encampment and had a $100,000 cleanup estimate
articles.summary: A long-standing dumping site in northeast Bexar County could soon be free of years of accumulated trash and debris, thanks to a volunteer-led cleanup
articles.body: A long-standing dumping site in northeast Bexar County could soon be free of years of accumulated trash and debris, thanks to a volunteer-led cleanup effort. The roughly half-acre property near Elm Cove Drive, between Walzem and Old Seguin roads, had become a persistent concern for nearby residents.The site, located near 7715 Elm Cove Drive outside Converse and bordering a residential neighborhood, was filled with discarded mattresses, a couch, a barbecue pit and other large items. Over four cleanup events, volunteers with River Aid San Antonio have removed approximately 43,000 pounds of trash from the property, according to KSAT.Volunteers tackle years of accumulated debrisVic Gomez, operations manager for River Aid San Antonio, said volunteers were shocked by the condition of the property when they first arrived.“For all of us, this was kind of a shock,” Gomez said. “When we first came here, we were walking through a lasagna layer of garbage that had accumulated over several years.”The property falls within the precinct of Bexar County Precinct 4 Commissioner Tommy Calvert. According to county officials, residents had complained about illegal dumping at the location for years.Libby Day, Calvert’s chief of staff, said the county had previously faced difficulties addressing the problem because officials were unable to contact the property owner.“This was formerly an encampment for folks who were suffering from homelessness,” Day said. “And one of the challenges with this site was the county was unable to get in contact with the property owner.”That situation has since changed, allowing the county to take additional steps to address the ongoing problems at the property.County works with Haven for Hope before enforcementAfter establishing contact with the property owner, the county was able to obtain consent for the Bexar County Sheriff’s Office to address illegal trespassing and dumping at the site.Before enforcement began, county officials also worked with Haven for Hope to connect people who had been staying at the property with shelter, services and other resources.“We did a lot of outreach with Haven for Hope, made sure folks got connected with services and resources,” Day said. “If they wanted to go to Haven, there were beds for them, and once that outreach took place, then enforcement started.”The county had initially received an estimated $100,000 quote to clean up the property using taxpayer funds. Day said that amount would have accounted for more than half of the county’s entire abatement budget.River Aid San Antonio helps reduce cleanup costsRather than relying solely on county funds, River Aid San Antonio stepped in to organize a volunteer cleanup effort.The response has brought together around 170 volunteers across four cleanup events, with residents from the surrounding neighborhood also joining the effort.“We’ve had a good handful of the neighbors come out to help us clean, and I think they’re very excited to help us make that difference,” Gomez said.The work has already removed 43,000 pounds of trash, significantly changing the appearance of the property and addressing a long-running concern for nearby residents.Final cleanup planned for NovemberRiver Aid San Antonio has one final cleanup event planned for Saturday, November 7, from 9 a.m. to noon.Volunteers are expected to meet at 7715 Elm Cove Drive to help complete the effort at the northeast Bexar County property.For residents who have lived near the site for years, the cleanup represents more than the removal of unwanted debris. articles.title: UK PM Andy Burnham rules out early general polls, says ‘no election anytime soon’
articles.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has ruled out an early general election, prioritizing the cost of living and support for businesses over election speculation. Despite recent polling suggesting Labour's rise under Burnham, he emphasizes a focus on governance rather than campaigning. The next general election is legally required by August 2029.
articles.body: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has ruled out calling an early general election, saying his focus is on tackling the cost of living and supporting businesses rather than putting the country through another election campaign.Speaking to BBC regional political editors ahead of the Labour Party conference in Liverpool, Burnham was asked whether he was considering an early poll.“No, not particularly. No, I’m not,” he said.“I see all the speculation and it just races ahead,” Burnham added. “No election anytime soon. I’m focused on the job as prime minister, doing what I said I would do.”Burnham was also asked whether a general election would be held next May alongside council elections in the East Midlands.“No,” he replied. “Not having a general election.”The comments come amid speculation that the government could call an early election, with reports that some advisers had been considering a poll as early as next year.Recent polling has suggested Labour's position has improved since Burnham replaced Sir Keir Starmer as prime minister in July, although Reform UK and the Conservatives remain close behind.Polling in recent weeks has shown a change in Labour's position since Burnham became prime minister in July, although Reform UK and the Conservatives have also remained competitive.The possibility of an early poll has also raised questions over whether Burnham could seek a fresh mandate and pursue priorities beyond those set out in Labour's 2024 manifesto. Under the current timetable, the next general election must be held by August 2029.Burnham is due to attend his first Labour Party conference as prime minister this weekend, where the prospect of a snap election is expected to be discussed by some party members.The prime minister said his priority was setting out the direction he wants to take the country rather than entering another election cycle.“The focus is on that, helping people with the cost of living, helping businesses with the cost of running a business,” he said.“These have got to be the priorities right now, rather than throwing the country into a backward-looking process where we're arguing again amongst ourselves.”Burnham said he wanted people to be “feeling a bit of hope in their lives again” and added that he wanted to take that work forward “rather than putting people back into an election cycle”.You use AI every day. articles.title: Researchers in Rwanda turn plastic waste into sisal-reinforced tiles; strongest sample reached 41.66 MPa with 0.225% water absorption
articles.summary: Plastic waste collected in Rwanda has been turned into experimental construction tiles that combine recycled thermoplastics with locally sourced sisal
articles.body: Plastic waste collected in Rwanda has been turned into experimental construction tiles that combine recycled thermoplastics with locally sourced sisal fibres. In a study published in Frontiers in Sustainability titled Manufacturing of plastic tiles based on reinforced sisal and recycled plastic wastes: a case of Rwanda, researchers at Rwanda Polytechnic-Ngoma College tested tiles made from recycled high-density polyethene, polyethene terephthalate, polypropylene, polyvinyl chloride and polystyrene, combined with sand, marble chips, cement and sisal. The strongest formulation, containing 5% sisal by volume, reached a mean compressive strength of 41.66 megapascals (MPa), while three tested tile samples recorded an average water absorption of just 0.225% after 24 hours of immersion.Rwanda's plastic waste problem provided the starting pointThe researchers developed the tiles against a persistent waste-management problem. Rwanda introduced a plastic-bag ban in 2008 and prohibited single-use plastics in 2019, but the study says substantial quantities of rigid post-consumer plastic remain outside formal collection and recycling systems. Citing previous research, the authors report that informal recyclers lack sufficient capacity and that about 70% of rigid plastic is left uncollected. The paper also points to plastic bottles clogging drainage systems in Kigali, contributing to flash flooding during heavy rain, and reports that microplastics have been detected in the Nyabarongo River. The researchers argue that converting discarded plastics into construction products could provide another route for handling material that might otherwise accumulate at disposal sites such as Nduba landfill.Five per cent sisal produced the strongest formulationThe team tested different levels of sisal reinforcement and found a clear increase in compressive strength as the fibre content rose. The control formulation without sisal reached 30.12 MPa, while mixtures containing 2%, 3% and 5% sisal reached 31.825, 37.705 and 41.66 MPa, respectively. The 5% formulation therefore represented a 38.3% increase over the 0% control, according to the researchers. The tested mixture was not simply plastic and fibre: the optimal formulation contained, by volume, 50.5% recycled plastic waste, 26.5% marble chips, 13% cement, 5% sisal fibres and 5% fine sand. The plastics were heated to between 200°C and 300°C, then mixed with the aggregate and sisal before being placed in wooden moulds and compressed while cooling.The recycled-plastic tiles absorbed very little waterThe tiles also performed strongly in the study's water-absorption test. Researchers dried the samples, immersed them in water for 24 hours and then compared their wet and dry masses. Three samples recorded absorption rates of 0.223%, 0.216% and 0.238%, producing a mean of 0.225%. The test followed ASTM D570, a standard method for measuring water absorption in plastics. The researchers attribute the low absorption partly to the hydrophobic plastic matrix, while the cement was intended to help bind the hydrophilic sisal and aggregate to the plastic and reduce internal voids. The result indicates strong resistance to water absorption under the specific laboratory conditions tested, although it does not by itself establish long-term performance in real buildings or outdoor environments.The researchers compared the tiles with ceramic and graniteThe paper also compares the experimental material with conventional ceramic and Nyagatare granite tiles used in Rwanda. The researchers report compressive strengths of roughly 20 to 30 MPa for ceramic tiles and 60 to 80 MPa for Nyagatare granite, while the experimental plastic tile reached 41.66 MPa. They also report water absorption of 0.5% to 7% for the ceramic comparison and about 0.1% for granite. In the study's cost comparison, the experimental tiles were estimated at 26,500 to 32,150 Rwandan francs per square metre, compared with 13,500 to 17,000 francs for ceramic and 36,000 to 45,400 francs for Nyagatare granite. These figures are the researchers' estimates and comparisons, rather than evidence of established market prices or a commercial cost advantage.The next challenge is moving beyond the laboratoryFor now, the material remains an experimental laboratory product rather than a demonstrated mass-produced building material. The researchers produced the tiles using a manual compression press and wooden moulds, with specimens allowed to remain under ambient laboratory conditions for seven days before testing. They suggest that industrial production would require more controlled equipment to improve mixing, fibre dispersion, moulding, and consistency. The study concludes that the 5% sisal formulation demonstrated technical feasibility under its tested conditions and recommends further research, including the use of artificial intelligence to predict cracking and fracture behaviour over the tiles' working life. That leaves durability, large-scale manufacturing and real-world performance as important questions for future testing.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Trump embraces Xi as peer, alarms partners and critics
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: A 48-hour state visit to the United States by China’s President Xi Jinping yielded no immediate major breakthroughs but
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: A 48-hour state visit to the United States by China’s President Xi Jinping yielded no immediate major breakthroughs but confirmed the broad impression, in visuals and much as words, that Washington now accepts China as a peer in a new G-2 formulation.For all the talk of trade, artificial intelligence, Taiwan, Iran and strategic competition, the most consequential message of Xi’s visit may have been the choreography itself. A fawning Trump repeatedly described Xi as a friend and the relationship as a “great friendship,” with little personal reciprocity from the Chinese leader.The charitable explanation for what many critics said was Trump’s folding before Xi and muting his demands from and tirades against China was purportedly in the service of American farmers – his major voting bloc – who are getting screwed because Beijing cut down purchase of soy, corn, and other farm produce. In brief remarks during a tea ceremony, the MAGA supremo mentioned that the visit had yielded “great results” for American farmers without elaborating, but spoke of little else other than accepting Xi’s invitation to visit China.By most accounts, the summit produced a lot of optics, but little else, amid a cascade of criticism that Trump is placating China rather than confronting it over its actions inimical to US, including its tacit support for Iran. The most withering censure came from Republican Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana, who likened Xi and leaders of Russia, North Korea and Iran, to reptiles. "The chief reptile, the quarterback, is President Xi. They all lie like timeshare salesmen. You can’t trust them. I wouldn’t turn my back on any of them, even if I thought and knew they were two days dead,” Kennedy told a TV show during the visit. Even Senator Chuck Grassley, the Iowa Republican whose state is deeply dependent on agricultural exports, was sceptical about the outcome of the visit, saying that if extending the trade truce was all that emerged, the summit risked becoming a “show job" for a communist autocrat.On Taiwan, the most sensitive strategic issue between the two sides, there was no public breakthrough. Trump has continued to hold in abeyance a roughly $14 billion Taiwan weapons package that he described earlier this year as a negotiating chip with Beijing. China wants the arms sales halted; US lawmakers across party lines have urged their release.Nor were there any signs of a significant Chinese concession on Iran. Beijing has expressed interest in peace and stability but remains economically intertwined with Tehran. On advanced chips, Washington also appeared to hold its line, despite Beijing’s interest in easing US technology restrictions. That may ultimately prove more consequential than the ceremonial theatrics. The summit thus produced no obvious quid pro quo in which China would use its leverage over Iran in return for a major American concession.Trump’s defenders argued though that the president’s approach should be judged against what they described as decades of failed China policy under previous administrations. “Obama and Biden talked tough, but gave away American factories to the Chinese. Trump actually launched a trade war against China,” noted Brian Kilmeade on Fox News, pointing out that Trump "kicked the Chinese out of Panama Canal" and went after their “favourite oil proxies in our hemisphere, Venezuela and Iran, and is about to kick them out of Cuba.”That in essence is the larger contradiction of the summit. Trump has not abandoned confrontation with China; he has instead recast it as transactional management between two superpowers, much to the consternation of other nations like India, Japan, and South Korea. Xi, for his part, repeatedly spoke not of friendship between two men but of China and the US as “two major countries” with a responsibility to find a new way of coexisting.The symbolism was perhaps captured most neatly by the contrasting tours offered during the two leaders’ encounters. When Trump visited Beijing in May, Xi showed him ancient trees at Zhongnanhai, including specimens more than 1,000 years old — a quiet display of Chinese historical depth and long-term continuity. In Washington, Trump showed Xi his new White House helipad, built in a “record” 12 weeks – which the Chinese would have built in 12 days if not 12 hours.You use AI every day. articles.title: At age 6, Grace Hendrian opened a lemonade stand hoping to raise $10 for the Salvation Army; seven summers later, she and sister June closed the project after turning that tiny goal into about $55,000
articles.summary: What began as a simple goal for a six-year-old to raise $10 for charity has now come to an end, leaving the local community with tens of thousands of
articles.body: What began as a simple goal for a six-year-old to raise $10 for charity has now come to an end, leaving the local community with tens of thousands of dollars in charitable support. Grace Hendrian and her younger sister, June, have finished the final season of their “Lemon-Aid Stand for Good” in Quincy, Illinois. What started as a small idea in 2019 grew into a fundraiser that brought in about $55,000 for The Salvation Army. WGEM reported that 2026 was the stand's final season.A modest ambition takes rootThe project began in 2019, when Grace was six years old and asked her mother, Kellea Hendrian, if she could run a lemonade stand and give the money to a local charity. Grace first set a goal of raising $10. Her father, Adam, suggested adding a zero and making the goal $100. The family ultimately raised more than $1,000 that first year. According to regional coverage from WGEM News, the first fundraiser far exceeded Grace's original goal. In 2019, the money donated to The Salvation Army's Family Services was enough to provide about 400 meals. In 2021, Grace's younger sister June joined the effort. Together, the sisters set out to raise enough money to provide 500 meals. The sisters gave all of the money they raised to The Salvation Army Quincy Area Command. The funds support Family Services programs that help people facing hunger, homelessness, and other hardships in the area.Expanding across the countyAs interest grew, the sisters turned the project from one lemonade stand into a community event. Beginning in 2022, Grace and June invited other children and families to run their own Lemon-Aid stands. Local groups, including churches and sports teams, could also take part. articles.title: Ramlilas Scripting New Chapter For Gen Z
articles.summary: Delhi Ramlilas target Gen Z with high-tech shows, live telecasts, tulsi saplings, theatre-style sound/LED staging and giant effigies for Oct festivities.
articles.body: New Delhi: Gen Z will be among the focus areas as Delhi’s Ramlilas prepare to return with a mix of tradition, technology and new ways of engaging younger audiences. From Tulsi saplings and towering effigies to immersive sound-and-light productions, organisers are combining spectacle with efforts to introduce youth to the values at the heart of the Ramayana.At Madhavdas Park, Red Fort Grounds, Shri Dharmik Leela Committee is preparing to present its 103-year-old Ramlila in a modern format while retaining the traditional Ram Katha. New staging elements and an expanded range of cultural and religious programmes are being planned to connect younger viewers with Indian culture.Committee spokesperson Ravi Jain said the presentation would evolve without losing its cultural essence. “Our aim from the beginning has been to introduce the youth to the life and character of Lord Ram. They should understand what he stood for and how he always upheld truth,” he said.Jain added younger generations may initially be attracted by the spectacle, but the experience could stay with them and gradually introduce them to the story’s deeper values. “If the messages of the Ramayana reach young people and they begin following these values, they can grow into responsible and principled citizens,” he added.Also at Red Fort Grounds, Lav Kush Ramlila Committee is placing Gen Z at the centre of its ‘Ghar-Ghar Ram, Ghar-Ghar Tulsi’ campaign. Committee president Arjun Kumar said Tulsi saplings would be distributed to 5,100 youngsters. “The Ramlila, scheduled from Oct 11 to 21, will feature a high-tech digital production and performances by around 40 Bollywood actors. It will also be telecast live. On Dussehra, an image of Lord Ram will be created using one lakh diyas,” Kumar said.Shri Ram Lila Committee Janakpuri, meanwhile, is experimenting with theatre-like technology. Its production will involve nearly 150 performers, expansive stages, arches, LED screens and a meticulously mapped sound system. “The person in the first row and someone in the last row will hear the performance with the same clarity. The basic concept remains unchanged, but we improve its presentation every year,” said Narendra Chawla, the committee’s general secretary.Based primarily on the Ramcharitmanas, the script also draws on other texts and depicts lesser-known episodes. “The narrative begins with Lord Shiva recounting Ram’s story to Parvati and returns to them during Ram’s coronation, completing the circle,” Chawla added.He added that actors from different Delhi theatre groups are selected through annual auditions instead of hiring a pre-assembled troupe. “We want to motivate the youth in the right direction. If even one person among the 50,000 watching is inspired to change, we believe our purpose has been fulfilled,” he said.Organisers of Ramlila at IP Extension said they were working to make this year’s production more engaging. Besides youngsters, teachers from several schools will also take part in performances, they said.In Dwarka Sector 10, scale will take centre stage as Dwarka Shri Ramlila Society prepares for its 15th edition. Its biggest attraction will be the burning of a 221-foot Ravan effigy. Chairman and chief patron Akash Rajesh Gehlot said the production would use its spectacle to convey the values of truth, righteousness, dignity and good conduct to the younger generation. articles.title: DDA issues notice on structural audit of highrises
articles.summary: DDA orders structural safety audits for Delhi highrises built or approved before March 21, 2001; owners have 3 months to comply or face legal action.
articles.body: New Delhi: Delhi Development Authority (DDA) has issued a circular asking owners or occupiers of highrise buildings that are 15m or higher, which have building plans sanctioned or construction done before March 21, 2001, to do a structural safety audit in the next three months.The authority, in a notice issued Thursday, clarified that a similar order was issued in July 2020. But the compliance was limited, prompting the authority to reissue the notice with a deadline, sources said.“The structural safety audit is mandatory to be carried out by the owners/occupiers of all highrise buildings (15m or above). Structural engineers empanelled with MCD or govt agencies are authorised to conduct the exercise. The fees and cost of the structural audit shall be borne by the owner or occupier,” the notice said.The authority has, however, clarified that getting permission to structurally upgrade or repair a building (retrofitting) does not mean govt is pardoning or approving any illegal construction or illegal activity on that property.Structural safety audits are also mandatory for buildings which were sanctioned before March 2001 and have a height of less than 15 metres with high public congregation. “Places include educational buildings, hospitals, institutional buildings, assembly buildings, cinema halls, malls and Group Housing,” the authority said.“In case of non-compliance within stipulated time, action against owner/property shall be initiated as per provisions contained in notification dated April 24, 2019, and Feb 10, 2020, of Govt of Delhi NCT,” the proposal said.These notifications were issued on the direction of Delhi High Court to mandate structural audits and implementation plans to make buildings in Delhi seismically compliant (earthquake-safe).Non-compliance amounts to legal penalties against the owner/occupier, such as criminal or civil prosecution for endangering public safety under applicable building regulations and bylaws. articles.title: After Kaushal’s house, another gangster’s property demolished in Gurgaon
articles.summary: Gurgaon police demolished illegal construction of gangster Krishan, a Kaushal Chaudhary gang member, in Naharpur Rupa during a crackdown on criminal properties.
articles.body: Gurgaon: An illegal construction belonging to a gangster was demolished in Naharpur Rupa on Friday. Krishan (31), who was involved in 11 criminal cases, has been convicted in three of them. The demolition of the house on Friday was carried out by the crime branch in coordination with the departments concerned. The action comes three days after the house of jailed gangster Kaushal Chaudhary was razed. The drive is part of a crackdown on properties allegedly linked to criminals and organised crime.Police said the illegal construction at Naharpur Rupa was identified on the basis of intelligence inputs. The land was cleared and restored to its original condition. “We will continue to carry out actions against land mafias, habitual offenders and their illegal construction network,” police spokesperson Sandeep Turan said.Krishan had been arrested by the Sector 39 crime branch team on July 6, 2025 from Naharpur Rupa in connection with an Arms Act case registered at Sadar police station. Two country-made pistols had been recovered. According to sources, Krishan’s criminal history includes an attempted murder and Arms Act case at Sadar police station in which he was convicted. He was also convicted in an Arms Act case registered at Rajendra Park police station for assaulting a public servant in 2019 and in a murder case registered at Badshahpur police station in the same year.On Tuesday, police, while clearing encroachment from govt land in Naharpur Rupa, demolished the house of Chaudhary, against whom a case was registered for the Aug 2021 murder of Youth Akali Dal leader Vicky Middukhera in Mohali. Vicky’s murder was allegedly linked to the killing of Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala by the Lawrence Bishnoi-Goldy Brar gang the following year. Chaudhary was also named in connection with the March 2022 killing of international kabaddi player Sandeep Nangal Ambian during a kabaddi match. articles.title: Arms, ammunition seized from former Ulfa-I militant’s house in Golaghat
articles.summary: Golaghat police seized 3 pistols, a modified AK-47 and live ammo from ex-ULFA-I militant Palash Jyoti Baruah’s house; he is absconding, probe on.
articles.body: Dibrugarh: Golaghat police on Friday seized three pistols, a modified AK-47 rifle and live ammunition during a search of the residence of former Ulfa-I militant Palash Jyoti Baruah at No. 2 Saraimari village in Merapani area of Golaghat district.In addition to the firearms and ammunition, police recovered a vehicle and a motorcycle from the premises.Police said Baruah, who surrendered in 2009 after being associated with the banned Ulfa-I, is currently absconding.Golaghat SSP Swapnaneel Deka said the search was conducted after police received specific information about the house.“We received specific intelligence input. Based on that information, a team led by our additional SP (headquarters), Bibhas Das, searched the house. From there, we recovered three pistols, a modified AK-47, some live ammunition, a vehicle, and a motorcycle,” Deka said.He added that police teams are making efforts to trace and apprehend Baruah.“This house belongs to a youth named Palash Jyoti Baruah. He is currently absconding, and our team is working actively to apprehend him. The seizure process is currently underway, and a team has been deployed to search for him,” the SSP said.Police are also probing the source of the seized weapons and the circumstances in which they were kept at the residence. Investigators suspect, but have not confirmed, that Baruah may have been involved in smuggling arms from Nagaland and supplying them to buyers in Assam.The seizure is significant as Golaghat district shares an interstate border with Nagaland, making the movement of people and contraband across the boundary a concern for law enforcement agencies.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.title: Influencer flaunts gold, cash on Insta; burglars make off with booty
articles.summary: Influencer’s Instagram reels showing gold, cash and travel plans may have tipped off burglars; ₹1 crore in jewellery stolen from Nagercoil home, police probe.
articles.body: Madurai: First came the Instagram reels showing off gold, bundles of currency and even money being showered on a child. Then came updates on where the family was heading to. By the time they returned from a shopping trip on Thursday night, jewellery worth about ₹1 crore had vanished from their house.The burglary was reported at the house of businessman Vinoth Kumar at Thamathukonam near Nagercoil in Kanyakumari district. Kumar, who is involved in several businesses including cardamom trade, lives there with his wife Madhumitha, a YouTube and Instagram influencer, and their child.The family left home on Thursday evening to shop for clothes and returned in the night. On entering the bedroom, Kumar found the bureau forced open and the valuables inside missing. The haul included 120 sovereigns of gold ornaments, diamond jewellery and ₹50,000 in cash. Kumar then alerted Rajakkamangalam police.Investigators found that the intruders had reached the house through the rear entrance. The lock had been sliced open with a cutting machine before they entered the bedroom and broke into the bureau.Police are now examining Madhumitha’s social-media activity as part of the investigation. Her videos had featured her wearing jewellery kept at home, displaying bundles of currency spread across a mattress and showering currency notes on her child.“She had also uploaded videos saying the family bought gold every month and posted updates about where they went to purchase jewellery. Other reels routinely disclosed where the family was travelling and the purpose of their outings,” said an investigating officer.Police said the timing of the burglary matched the family’s Instagram updates, indicating the burglars tracked the reels and struck when the house was vacant. “Kanyakumari SP (Anshul Nagar) visited the crime scene and five special teams have been formed to track the suspects,” said inspector Jayalakshmi.Madhumitha had earlier courted controversy after entering the sanctum area of Suchindram Thanumalayan Swamy temple and filming a video. articles.title: 30 evacuated as fire breaks out at Model Town food outlet
articles.summary: 30 evacuated after a fire at a Model Town-II food outlet in Delhi; suspected short circuit. 23 firefighting units deployed to contain medium blaze.
articles.body: New Delhi: Thirty people were evacuated after a fire broke out at a food outlet in northwest Delhi’s Model Town Thursday afternoon. Police suspect a short circuit may have triggered the blaze.The fire was reported around 1.58pm at a food outlet in Model Town-II. A beat officer from Model Town police station, among the first responders, alerted senior officers, following which a police team rushed to the spot.On reaching the site, police found smoke billowing from the premises and immediately began evacuating people from the outlet and adjoining buildings as a precautionary measure. A total of 30 people were safely moved to safety, police said.Fire department teams were also mobilised and initially deployed two water tenders and two water bowser vehicles. The incident was later categorised as a medium fire, prompting the deployment of additional resources.According to fire officials, 23 firefighting units, including nine water tenders and nine water bowser vehicles, were pressed into service to contain the blaze and prevent it from spreading to nearby structures.Police said the fire is suspected to have been caused by a short circuit.In Aug, five people were rescued by Delhi Fire Services and local residents after a fire broke out in an air-conditioner installed in a hotel kitchen in Rohini.
